anomalies.observed: Schematic shows U1 pin 6 (A) and pin 7 (B) connected together to the same net labelled TTL.
anomalies.expected: Per the design spec, the MAX3485 A and B pins are differential lines; they should be separate, with R6 providing a pull-up on A and R8/R15 providing a pull-down on B, not shorted together.

evidence.quote: U1 pins 6 and 7 tied together to net TTL
R6, R7, R8, R15 ... Bias/pull network on the MAX3485 A/B differential lines

anomalies.impact: Shorting the RS-485 driver outputs prevents proper differential signaling and may damage U1; serial servo communication will fail.

anomalies.observed: C1 and C4 are labelled 100n (100 nF) on the servo power rail.
anomalies.expected: Spec says C1–C4 are 100 µF ×4 bulk capacitance on the servo power rail.

evidence.quote: C1–C4 | 100 µF × 4 | Bulk capacitance on the servo power rail

anomalies.impact: Reduced bulk capacitance may allow servo inrush current to dip the 5V rail, causing M5Stack brownouts or resets.

anomalies.observed: The TXD2 net is connected to J1/J2 pin 13.
anomalies.expected: Spec says TXD2/RXD2 are on J1/J2 pins 15/16, so TXD2 should be on pin 15.
anomalies.impact: The UART TX line is routed to the wrong M5Stack bus pin, so serial servo communication will not work.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains several deviations from the intended design: the MAX3485 A/B outputs are shorted together, C1/C4 are 100 nF instead of 100 µF, and TXD2 is routed to bus pin 13 instead of pin 15.
